original.target_description: Study 1: omnibus repeated-measures effect of facial emotion (happy, neutral, angry) on anterior-posterior body-sway variability (SD-AP), female students. This identifies the emotion/body-sway test, but supplied p.4 locator instead shows a representative participant plot, so exact intended-test match remains unverified.

n.sample_role: Female student participants in repeated-measures body-sway analysis; exact analytic n not explicitly printed.
n.exclusions: Three participants identified as excessive-movement outliers (body-sway Z scores >4); analyzed n not stated explicitly.
n.location: Printed pp.1576–1577 (PDF pp.2–3), Method/Participants and Results opening.
n.quote: Fifty female students (mean age = 20.6 years, SD = 2.3 years) were included in this study. / Three participants were identified as outliers because of their excessive movements, as reflected in Z scores greater than 4 on the body-sway measure.

es.location: Printed p.1577 (PDF p.3), Body sway, first sentence.
es.quote: An ANOVA for SD-AP yielded a significant effect of emotion, … F(2, 45) = 5.20, p = .009, ηp2 = .19.

p.location: Printed p.1577 (PDF p.3), Body sway, first sentence.

replication.target_description: Replication study 1 measured heart rate only; target body-sway relationship was not measured. The heart-rate block ANOVA is not the body-sway test.

notes:
Replication p. 1891 (PDF p. 2): "First, we focused on heart rate and did not include a measure of body sway." Supplied replication locator p. 3 contains heart-rate analyses, not the target body-sway outcome. No analytic n, effect size, or p attributed to a nonexistent body-sway replication test. Original acquisition failure details are in texts/03c1fec331b10ea539fdbd6d.miss.
Source follow-up: Published seven-page article, Facing Freeze: Social Threat Induces Bodily Freeze in Humans, Roelofs, Hagenaars, and Stins (2010), DOI 10.1177/0956797610384746; first page and PDF pages 3–5 visually inspected. The supplied p.4 (printed p.1578) contains Figure 2 only, showing an individual body-sway path; the omnibus emotion effect is printed on PDF p.3. Extracted the uniquely described omnibus emotion/body-sway result, but target_match is null because the locator does not directly establish that selection. Analytic n left null rather than substituting the total recruited sample or calculating n from degrees of freedom. No metric conversion.
